title: II. By the light of nature: Gentiles both barbarians and philosophers acknowledge immortality and care about the soul's state after this life
pass_a_gloss: II. By the light belonging toward nature: because that same has stood as received by common opinion so that the Gentiles — both barbarians and philosophers — have acknowledged this, and on that account have stood as anxious concerning its state after this life.
pass_b_english: II. By the light of nature: because it has been received by common opinion that the Gentiles — both barbarians and philosophers — have acknowledged this, and on that account have been anxious about its state after this life.
source_text: II. Luce naturae, quia communi id opinione receptum est, ut gentiles tum barbari, tum philosophi agnoverint, hacque propter de ejus post hanc vitam statu soliciti fuerint.
